title: Morning Edition
intro: Today’s briefing covers product launches, a major corporate AI rollout, a high-profile policy pledge that drew criticism, and a security flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac app. These items touch product features, enterprise scale, investor focus, and software risk.

items.title: OpenAI Launches Virtual Try-on In ChatGPT
items.why: Adds a new consumer-facing capability to ChatGPT that blends conversational AI with product visualization.
items.headline: OpenAI adds virtual try-on to ChatGPT
items.aiSummary: OpenAI launched a virtual try-on feature in ChatGPT. Virtual try-on allows users to simulate trying products inside the ChatGPT app.

items.title: Barclays Scales Anthropic’s Claude AI to 16,000 Employees and Global Developer Teams
items.why: Represents a large enterprise deployment of a third-party AI model across employees and engineering teams.
items.headline: Barclays scales Anthropic’s Claude to 16,000 employees
items.aiSummary: Barclays has scaled Anthropic’s Claude AI across 16,000 employees and its global developer teams. The rollout expands internal use and developer access to Claude at the bank.

items.title: Trump’s ‘self-policing’ AI accord faces skepticism
items.summary: The signing of an AI accord by President Trump and tech leaders has done little to quell concerns over the lack of guardrails surrounding artificial intelligence. While Trump says industry officials can self-police, critics say more is needed to make sure AI development doesn’t get out of hand, even as some described it as a...
items.why: Signals ongoing tension between industry-led commitments and calls for stronger oversight of AI.
items.headline: Trump’s self-policing AI accord draws skepticism
items.aiSummary: President Trump and tech leaders signed an AI accord that relies on industry self-policing. Critics say the agreement has done little to calm concerns about the lack of guardrails and argue more is needed to prevent AI development getting out of hand.

items.title: AI music maker Suno now generates spoken words
items.summary: Suno is branching out from the world of AI music, launching a new feature that generates spoken voices based on scripts or prompted descriptions. Speech is now available in public beta across Suno's web and mobile platforms, and allows you to simultaneously generate voiceovers and background music to accompany them. items.why: Expands an AI music maker into speech generation, combining voice and music in one workflow.
items.headline: Suno adds spoken-word generation in public beta
items.aiSummary: Suno launched a feature that generates spoken voices from scripts or prompted descriptions and put speech into public beta on web and mobile. The tool lets users generate voiceovers and background music simultaneously.

items.title: 4 Key Questions for Investors to Ask at the Start of Q4
items.why: Provides a concise checklist for investors preparing for the new quarter.
items.headline: Morningstar publishes four investor questions for Q4
items.aiSummary: Morningstar released a piece titled '4 Key Questions for Investors to Ask at the Start of Q4.' The article frames investor considerations for the fourth quarter.

items.title: A Flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac App Could Have Let Hackers Grab Sensitive Data
items.summary: While the focus has been on AI agents’ hacking capabilities, a recently patched vulnerability in a ChatGPT app shows that AI software is itself an inviting—and vulnerable—target.
items.why: Underscores software security risks in widely used AI applications and the need for timely patches.
items.headline: ChatGPT Mac app flaw could have exposed sensitive data
items.aiSummary: A recently patched vulnerability in the ChatGPT Mac app could have allowed hackers to grab sensitive data. The flaw highlights that AI software itself is an inviting and vulnerable target.
